hook: An FBI-submitted monochrome photograph showing a dark circular object centered on a crosshair reticle, taken from a U.S. government imaging system over what appears to be ground terrain. The operator could not positively identify the object, and both the date and location have been withheld.
why_it_matters: This photograph represents one of a small number of UAP images formally submitted by the FBI to AARO under the disclosure framework, notable because the FBI is a domestic law enforcement agency rather than a military or intelligence collection body. The use of a reticle-equipped imaging system suggests the object was deliberately tracked or targeted for observation. The redaction of date and location—combined with the absence of any mission report—leaves the operational context entirely opaque.

key_findings.finding: The FBI submitted this image to AARO as a UAP report, derived from an unspecified U.S. government imaging system.
A dark, circular object appears precisely at the center of the crosshair reticle, suggesting the object was actively tracked or framed by the imaging operator.
The original imagery was redacted before submission to AARO, meaning AARO itself received an altered version rather than raw source material.
No mission report was provided alongside the image, and the operator formally reported an inability to positively identify the object.
Both the date and location of the event are withheld, making temporal and geographic correlation with other UAP reports impossible from this record alone.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The FBI submitted this photograph directly to AARO as part of the formal UAP reporting pipeline described in the manifest.

The use of a reticle-equipped government imaging system with redacted provenance raises questions about the originating collection platform, which may fall under technical intelligence collection programs.
